scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The three imported Alans IDs share a broad cultural narrative, not an assertion that one kingdom persisted from antiquity through the medieval period. The map intervals 100 to 200, 700 to 800, and 1000 to 1200 are separate snapshot coverage.

The 1100 to 1200 geometry for alans-1000 includes a detached Lower Danube and Balkan polygon as well as North Caucasian territory. The narrative does not certify that polygon or claim medieval royal control there. No borders are modified.
The queue assigns these IDs to Europe; this packet concerns the North Caucasian and European Alans. It does not replace Qwen’s Asia assignment or produce a separate Asian polity card.

The 1985 Iranica entry and 2025 Latham-Sprinkle monograph differ in their political chronology and model of identity. The ending follows the newer study’s explicit argument that fragmentation preceded Mongol invasion, attributed to its author. Iranica is used for ancient attestations, dispersal and linguistic records, not its Catalonia etymology, Arthurian theory, obsolete population number or a simple unified-state model.

The historical period divisions are approximate organizing phases. The fourth-century Roman account is dated to its approximate composition, not invented as a single event in Alan life. Its contemptuous judgments and sweeping claims are not adopted.

The Met’s current catalog dates the kaftan to the seventh to ninth centuries, while the 2001 study used eighth to tenth centuries. The card follows the current catalog and records this difference. Moshchevaja Balka is a probable attribution, not an excavated context for this particular purchase.

The kaftan catalog and Harper provenance account together are kept below a 200-word paraphrase-and-note budget. The conservation newsletter is a separate research account. The coat’s apparent completeness is not presented as wholly original survival.

The terrace paper’s abstract and the soil paper’s indexed publisher abstract/conclusion support only the reported findings used here. The paywalled full soil article was not read. No crop species, yields, field ownership system or population counts are inferred.
Cultural and linguistic continuity does not establish exclusive biological ancestry, modern territorial rights or genetic uniformity. No unsupported successor target is linked.
Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
